messages.text: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

Automotive radar echo generation is moving into dynamic artificial-object generation with hybrid and fully digital concepts, including digital operation for FMCW radar and generated distances up to 3000 m [4].
That increases VNA needs on the IF side because the AREG800A platform has IF bandwidth options from 1 GHz to 2 GHz and 5 GHz, and its production configuration can use 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth [5][8].
The supported VNA measurement spans for AREG800A IF transfer characteristics scale accordingly: 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz, with 2.5 MHz frequency steps, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, and –10 dBm source power [7].
For ghost-object suppression, the required VNA capability includes time-domain measurement, 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and the same IF spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [6].
VNAs that can address these broader or higher-frequency needs include R&S ZNA models up to 67 GHz, with base measurement bandwidth from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz and an option up to 30 MHz, plus time-domain analysis and mmWave converter support options [20][25].
For still higher-frequency measurement, the R&S ZNA67EXT system covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz with 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz measurement bandwidths [57].
【推論】As automotive radar test setups use wider IF bandwidths such as 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, the VNA must support wider IF-span characterization up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz rather than only narrower 1 GHz or 2 GHz spans.[5][7][8]
【推論】As testing emphasizes artificial objects and ghost-object suppression, the VNA must support time-domain analysis with fine frequency stepping, because the AREG800A ghost-object measurement condition explicitly uses a vector network analyzer in time domain with 125 kHz step size.[6]

Automotive radar echo generation is moving into dynamic artificial-object generation with hybrid and fully digital concepts, including digital operation for FMCW radar and generated distances up to 3000 m [4].
That increases VNA needs on the IF side because the AREG800A platform has IF bandwidth options from 1 GHz to 2 GHz and 5 GHz, and its production configuration can use 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth [5][8].
The supported VNA measurement spans for AREG800A IF transfer characteristics scale accordingly: 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz, with 2.5 MHz frequency steps, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, and –10 dBm source power [7].
For ghost-object suppression, the required VNA capability includes time-domain measurement, 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power, and the same IF spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [6].
VNAs that can address these broader or higher-frequency needs include R&S ZNA models up to 67 GHz, with base measurement bandwidth from 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz and an option up to 30 MHz, plus time-domain analysis and mmWave converter support options [20][25].
For still higher-frequency measurement, the R&S ZNA67EXT system covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz with 1 Hz to 1.5 MHz measurement bandwidths [57].
【推論】As automotive radar test setups use wider IF bandwidths such as 5 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, the VNA must support wider IF-span characterization up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz rather than only narrower 1 GHz or 2 GHz spans.[5][7][8]
【推論】As testing emphasizes artificial objects and ghost-object suppression, the VNA must support time-domain analysis with fine frequency stepping, because the AREG800A ghost-object measurement condition explicitly uses a vector network analyzer in time domain with 125 kHz step size.[6]
